decisive_items: capillaroscopy image description: late signs with avascular areas
response.rationale: The combination of skin thickening, Raynaud phenomenon, salt-and-pepper lesions, interstitial lung disease, pulmonary hypertension, and capillaroscopy avascular areas is highly specific for systemic sclerosis. Other candidates lack these pathognomonic features; MCTD is a possible overlap but lacks anti-U1 RNP and the scleroderma-specific findings dominate.

rejected.why: Weak anti-Sm and ANA are present, but the skin, lung, and capillaroscopy findings are not typical of SLE; the overall pattern is scleroderma.
Arthritis and morning stiffness are present, but the systemic sclerosis features (skin thickening, Raynaud, ILD) are not explained by RA.
Sicca symptoms and Schirmer test are supportive, but they are secondary to the underlying systemic sclerosis; no anti-SSA/SSB.
Overlap features exist, but the absence of anti-U1 RNP and the presence of specific scleroderma skin and lung findings make MCTD less likely.
